Well I tried OSI Quad Max instead of DAP 3.0 and I fucking love this stuff. Comes out much smooth and tools much easier without leaving the ripples and lift off marks DAP does. This will be my go to exterior caulk from now on. You can also color match it which is useful. If I ever get new siding or build a house from scratch I will probably go with PPG pre-finished LP smartside, and OSI Quad Max color matched to PPG. For the trim possibly Miratec PVC or Smartside.

I have a scrap of smartside trim that I am going to leave somewhere damp and see how it handles moisture. It's treated with zinc borate which is good stuff in itself. Borate is popular in New Zealand for their wet weather, I've used a product called Tim-bor before to treat wood. It's a borate salt you mix in to solution and spray on to wood. You can also sprinkle it around to kill insects.

There are actually 2 kinds of smartside; "strand" and "fiber", the fiber is shit but the strand stuff is quite good IMO. It's basically OSB with extra resins and zinc borate and pressed with a cedar grain and pre-primed. A good system would be using Huber Zip sheathing, the Zip system butyl membrane flashing tape, Grace Vycor ice dam membrane on roof/wall intersections and along gutters. I'm a big fan on the Huber Zip system. Couple that with "Slicker" rainscreen wrap that always drainage/ventilation behind the siding boards and I think it would be a good system if the paint is kept up. Although I'm not sure if the siding might bend with a rainscreen if the nails aren't driven perfectly. I'd have to research it. Smartside has a 5 year warranty so I'm assuming painting every 5 years would be advisable, and some HOAs even have a 5 year re-paint rule in their covenants. Sherman Williams Duration seems like a good exterior paint.

I'm going to go buy some of the regular OSI Quad which I think doesn't have the silicon added like the Quad Max does, it's closer to regular polyurethane I believe.
